source.excerpt: When I feed the hungry, they call me a saint.
trail: Wikiquote’s Dorothy Day page places the sentence under Misattributed, credits Câmara, and cites John Dear’s Peace Behind Bars (1995), p. 65. The book page was not inspected here.

The Centro internazionale Helder Camara’s biography attributes a close food-and-Communist variant to Câmara. Medical Missionaries of Mary independently publishes another English variant with his name.
The underlying saying is consistently associated with Câmara. No single original occasion or definitive translator for the displayed English version was established.

author.name: Hélder Câmara
author.heading: About Hélder Câmara
author.bio: Hélder Câmara (1909–1999) was a Brazilian Catholic archbishop of Olinda and Recife and an advocate for poor communities and human rights. His public work under Brazil’s military regime connected direct help with criticism of social inequality, earning him both international recognition and political hostility.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The saying contrasts providing immediate help with asking why deprivation persists. That contrast fits Câmara’s public advocacy for poor communities and social justice in Brazil. Dorothy Day’s own commitment to the poor helps explain the appeal of the mistaken credit, but thematic affinity is not authorship evidence.

schema.faqAnswer: The saying is associated with Brazilian archbishop Hélder Câmara, not Dorothy Day. Wikiquote flags the Day credit; several English versions circulate, and the original occasion and translator of this exact wording remain unconfirmed.
